SafePal has experienced a data breach affecting approximately 39,798 customers, with personal order information being sold on a cybercrime forum. The breach involved unauthorized access to sensitive customer data, but it did not compromise users' wallet funds or passwords. SafePal is currently investigating the incident and has implemented additional security measures to prevent future occurrences.

 - SafePal's data breach has exposed personal order information for nearly 40,000 customers.
 - The stolen data may be used for targeted phishing attacks against affected individuals.

Source: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/safepal-data-breach-impacts-39-798-customers-stolen-info-for-sale/

A new malware called AmnesiaStealer has emerged, targeting macOS users and allowing attackers to control victims' web browsers and access authenticated sessions. This malware exploits vulnerabilities in Chromium-based browsers to steal sensitive information, including passwords and cryptocurrency data. Researchers have noted its sophisticated capability to remotely control the browser while maintaining the integrity of user profiles.

 - AmnesiaStealer targets macOS users through ClickFix attacks, allowing live control over browsers.
 - The malware can exfiltrate sensitive data from 16 Chromium-based browsers, including authentication credentials and cryptocurrency information.

Source: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-amnesiastealer-macos-malware-hijacks-browser-sessions-via-remote-control/

 - PJM has incurred $12 billion in excessive costs due to inaccurate modeling of electricity demand and supply.
 - PJM's upcoming emergency auction seeks to address capacity shortfalls but may financially burden ratepayers.
 - The system's design has led to substantial price spikes and inadequate connection timelines for new power plants.

Recent advancements in the field of gravitational lensing and microlensing of supernovae have opened new avenues for exploring cosmology and astrophysics. The ability to use time delays between multiple images of strongly lensed supernovae to measure cosmological distances could provide critical constraints on cosmological parameters, including the Hubble constant. Upcoming surveys, particularly from the Rubin Observatory, are expected to significantly increase the number of lensed supernovae discoveries, enabling a deeper understanding of their properties and impacts on galaxy studies.

 - Strong gravitational lensing and microlensing of supernovae are emerging tools for measuring cosmological distances.
 - The upcoming Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time is anticipated to significantly enhance the discovery of lensed supernovae.

Source: https://infoscience.epfl.ch/entities/publication/644cad8a-6c9b-4b02-bcf3-b8b6e8c614c5

Prolly is an open-source library designed to provide an efficient content-addressed ordered map using prolly trees, which allow for immutable snapshots, cheap branching, and efficient diffs and merges. It offers features like asynchronous support, structural sharing, and transaction-safe updates, making it suitable for applications requiring comprehensive data management capabilities. The library also supports various backends for data storage, allowing developers to choose the implementation that best fits their needs.

 - Prolly implements scalable data structures that enhance operational efficiency for applications.
 - The library supports both synchronous and asynchronous operations for diverse application requirements.
 - Prolly can be integrated with multiple backends to enable flexible and durable data storage options.

Source: https://github.com/crabbuild/prolly
